rule.description: One locally defined type acts as the crate's god class: inherent impl blocks for that single type appear in several module files of the crate, or the type has accumulated more inherent methods (across all files) than a cohesive type in this codebase plausibly owns. Inherent impls for the same type in 3 or more distinct module files trip the ownership-boundary clause; 12 or more total inherent methods trip the sheer-size clause. Only inherent impls defined in the crate and written directly in real module files count: trait impls and macro-generated impls never do.
rule.checker: Dylint rule library `multi_module_impl_god_class` (rustc late-lint pass, MULTI_MODULE_IMPL_GOD_CLASS), one diagnostic per module file that carries an impl block of the flagged type

checks.description: Locates every module file that owns an inherent impl block for a type flagged by the god-class rule, and enumerates the methods implemented there versus the type's total footprint.
checks.detected_relation: type -> inherent impl blocks for the same type appearing in several module files, or a single type accumulating an oversized set of inherent methods
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The flagged type has absorbed responsibilities that belong to the other modules: they can no longer be read, tested, or changed in isolation from the type that centralized everything. The writer-side type of this crate participates in construction, reader provisioning, epoch bookkeeping, guard issuance, and factory minting through impls placed in five different module files.

matches.evidence: The crate root hosts builder entry points for the writer type: two inherent methods (`from_value`, `from_default`) constructing the writer/reader pair and registering the initial reader, implemented far from both the write-path machinery and the epoch table they coordinate.

The reader module hosts two writer-type methods: `spawn_reader` registers an additional reader on the writer's epoch table, and `snapshot_reader_epochs` mirrors reader epoch progress into the writer's own state.
The factory module hosts `reader_factory`, which mints a cross-thread reader factory from the writer's internals; constructing that factory reaches directly into writer-owned and reader-owned fields.

The guard module hosts `enter_read_guard`, a writer-side entry into the read path that manipulates reader-private epoch/enter counters directly; it is implemented alongside a new private helper `ReadGuard::enter_state` that exposes guard internals to this cross-module caller.

The type's home module retains the whole write path (11 inherent methods) and its fields were widened to crate visibility so that the four foreign impl blocks can manipulate the writer's shared epoch state, the reader handle it holds, and its last-known reader epochs from any module.

excluded.reason: Alias/facade methods stay in and are owned by the aliasing module itself; the type does not cross module ownership boundaries and stays below the rule's size clause, so it is intentionally not part of this case.
The read-side handle keeps cohesive reader behavior inside the reader module and stays below both thresholds; it is the well-factored counter-example to the flagged type.
Gained a small helper for cross-module guard entry but remains a single-module, two-method type; it does not by itself satisfy the rule.
Write-path internal log type; its behavior lives in a single module and it is not flagged by the rule.
Custom-operation trait: trait impls and trait definitions are never counted by this rule, which measures only inherent impls.
